title: Get Maximum in Generated Array
notes:
## Intuition

Every rule reads only entries with smaller indices: `nums[2i]` reads `nums[i]`, and `nums[2i + 1]` reads `nums[i]` and `nums[i + 1]`, both below `2i + 1` for `i >= 1`. So the array can be filled from left to right in one pass while tracking the maximum. Computing each entry by recursion from the rules also works but repeats work; with `n <= 100` either is fast, and the simulation is the clean answer.

## Approach

1. If `n` is `0`, the array is just `[0]`: return `0`.
2. Create `nums` with `n + 1` slots, set `nums[1] = 1`, and start `best` at `1`.
3. For each `i` from `2` to `n`, let `half = floor(i / 2)`. An even `i` copies `nums[half]`; an odd `i` adds `nums[half]` and `nums[half + 1]`.
4. Update `best` after each entry and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 7`. Start with `nums[0] = 0`, `nums[1] = 1`, `best = 1`.

- `i = 2`: even, `nums[2] = nums[1] = 1`.
- `i = 3`: odd, `nums[3] = nums[1] + nums[2] = 2`, `best = 2`.
- `i = 4`: `nums[4] = nums[2] = 1`.
- `i = 5`: `nums[5] = nums[2] + nums[3] = 3`, `best = 3`.
- `i = 6`: `nums[6] = nums[3] = 2`; `i = 7`: `nums[7] = nums[3] + nums[4] = 3`.

`nums = [0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3]` and the answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one constant-time step per index.
- Space: O(n) for `nums`.

## Pitfalls

- `n = 0` has no index `1`; returning `best = 1` there would be wrong.
- For odd `i`, `half` is `(i - 1) / 2`; use `Math.floor(i / 2)` rather than `i / 2`, which is a fraction in JavaScript.
- The maximum is not always the last entry (for `n = 6`, `nums[6] = 2` but `nums[5] = 3`), so track it over the whole array.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nums` | the generated array |
| `best` | largest value generated so far |
| `i` | index being filled |
| `half` | `floor(i / 2)`, the index the rule reads from |

narration.2: With n = 0 the array is just [0], so the answer is 0.
narration.5: Make room for indices 0 to n; nums[0] stays 0.
narration.6: The second base value: nums[1] is 1.
narration.7: The largest value so far is nums[1] = 1.
narration.8: Fill the remaining indices in increasing order; each rule reads only earlier entries.
narration.9: Both rules read from index floor(i / 2).
narration.10: Even indices copy the entry at half.
narration.13: Odd indices add the entries at half and half + 1.
narration.17: Return the largest value in the generated array.
